finding.claim: The /invoice/<inv_id> route returns any invoice by ID with no ownership check (IDOR / broken object-level authorization). The sibling /my/invoice route enforces inv['customer'] == g.user['id'], so the unguarded route looks like an oversight.
finding.source: The inv_id URL path parameter, supplied by any requester. The route has no authentication or ownership precondition.
finding.sink: jsonify(inv) returns the full invoice record, which belongs to another customer.

trace.note: Route /invoice/<inv_id> is registered with no auth decorator.
INVOICES.get(inv_id) fetches the record by attacker-supplied key. There is no comparison against g.user.
The full invoice is serialized and returned.

finding.guards_checked: There is no before_request hook, login_required decorator or other auth middleware in the file. The ownership check at line 16 exists only on /my/invoice. The file defines no other guard. g.user is never set in this file, so any authentication would have to come from external code that is not present. Even if such code authenticates the caller, this route never compares the invoice owner to the caller.

verdict.reason: invoices.py:7-10 serves INVOICES.get(inv_id) via jsonify with no auth decorator, before_request hook or owner comparison, unlike the check at invoices.py:16 on /my/invoice, so any requester can read any invoice by ID.

verdict_facts.reason: invoices.py:7-10 serves INVOICES.get(inv_id) via jsonify with no decorator or g.user ownership comparison, unlike the check at invoices.py:16 on the sibling route, so any HTTP client can read any invoice by ID.
